plugin-settings.title: Social Login Settings
plugin-settings.setup-guide-title: How to set up Social Login
plugin-settings.setup-guide-desc: Enable a provider, then create an OAuth application in that provider's developer console. Copy the Client ID and Client Secret here, and register the Redirect URI shown below in the provider console.
plugin-settings.redirect-base-url-desc: Public origin of your site (e.g. https://example.com). Leave empty to use the platform website URL.
plugin-settings.reveal-desc: Enter your password to view the client secret.
plugin-settings.redirect-uri-desc: Register this exact URI in the provider's developer console.

guide.heading: Setup guide
guide.intro: To enable {provider}, create an OAuth app in its developer console and copy the Client ID & Secret here. Step by step:

guide-notes.google:
Open the Google Cloud Console and create or select a project.
Go to 'APIs & Services → OAuth consent screen' and configure it (User type 'External', app name, support email).
Go to 'APIs & Services → Credentials → Create credentials → OAuth client ID' and pick application type 'Web application'.
Under 'Authorized redirect URIs' add the Redirect URI shown below (it must match exactly), then click Create.
Copy the shown Client ID and Client Secret into the fields above.
guide-notes.discord:
Open the Discord Developer Portal and click 'New Application'; give it a name.
Open the 'OAuth2' tab in the left menu.
Copy the Client ID and Client Secret from 'OAuth2 → General' into the fields above (use 'Reset Secret' if no secret is shown).
Under 'OAuth2 → Redirects' click 'Add Redirect', paste the Redirect URI shown below and save.
guide-notes.facebook:
Open Meta for Developers → 'My Apps' → 'Create app' and choose a type that includes Facebook Login.
Add the 'Facebook Login' product to the app.
In 'App settings → Basic' copy the App ID (Client ID) and App Secret (Client Secret) into the fields above.
In 'Facebook Login → Settings' add the Redirect URI shown below to 'Valid OAuth Redirect URIs' and save.
Switch the app to 'Live' mode so real users (not only testers) can sign in.
guide-notes.twitter:
Open the X Developer Portal and create a Project, then an App inside it.
In the app open 'User authentication settings' and click 'Set up'.
Enable 'OAuth 2.0', set 'Type of App' to 'Web App' (confidential client) and add the Redirect URI shown below as the Callback URI; fill the website URL and save.
Open 'Keys and tokens' and copy the OAuth 2.0 Client ID and Client Secret into the fields above.
guide-notes.github:
Open GitHub 'Settings → Developer settings → OAuth Apps' and click 'New OAuth App'.
Fill in the application name and homepage URL.
Set 'Authorization callback URL' to the Redirect URI shown below.
Click 'Register application', copy the Client ID, then 'Generate a new client secret' and copy it into the fields above.
guide-notes.twitch:
Open the Twitch Developer Console → 'Applications' → 'Register Your Application'.
Fill in the name and category.
Set 'OAuth Redirect URLs' to the Redirect URI shown below.
Create the app, copy the Client ID, then click 'New Secret' and copy both into the fields above.
guide-notes.instagram:
Open Meta for Developers → 'Create app' and choose a 'Business' app.
Add the 'Instagram' product and pick 'Instagram API with Instagram Login'.
In the API setup add the Redirect URI shown below to the OAuth redirect URIs.
Copy the Instagram app ID (Client ID) and Instagram app secret (Client Secret) into the fields above.
Add Instagram testers (or submit for App Review) — only added testers can sign in until the app is approved.
